Production's usage limits, as `npx convex deployment usage-limits list --prod --json` prints them: an active `warning` limit on some metric, and on `aiGatewayCostDollars` too when models go through the Convex AI Gateway (`@convex-dev/ai-sdk-provider` installed). A limit past its threshold warns. Limits that cannot be read pass, saying so.

| Capability | Title | In dev | Under `--prod` | `--fix` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `monitoring` | Usage alerts | Not checked | Warns, never fails | No |

**Why it matters:** The deployment cannot read its own usage, so the backend raises no alert for it: Convex's `warning` usage limit is the alert, an email to the team on a production deployment, before a bill or a `disable` limit that pauses the whole app. **Fix:** Set one with `npx convex deployment usage-limits set --prod --metric functionCalls --window month --type warning --limit <calls>`, and `--metric aiGatewayCostDollars` in dollars for the gateway ([Alerts](/docs/ship/operate/monitoring#alerts)). Check it again with `npx nuxt-backend doctor --only monitoring --prod`.

analytics-metrics.title: Billing metrics
analytics-metrics.entry:
### `analytics-metrics`

The billing access token visible here reads the provider's metrics: a read of their date limits, which takes the `metrics:read` scope. No token here is `billing-access`'s finding, so this one is not reported then.

| Capability | Title | In dev | Under `--prod` | `--fix` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analytics` | Billing metrics | Warns, never fails | Still a warning | No |

**Why it matters:** The admin console's Revenue view reads the provider's metrics each time it opens. Without the scope, every read is refused as `unavailable` ([Read revenue and usage](/docs/build/growth/measure/revenue)). **Fix:** Issue an organization access token with the `metrics:read` scope besides the ones it has, put it in `.env.local`, and run `npx nuxt-backend env push`. Check it again with `npx nuxt-backend doctor --only analytics`.

analytics-activation.title: Activation event
analytics-activation.entry:
### `analytics-activation`

The event kind of the app's own (`app.…`) that `setupAudit({ activation })` names in `backend/audit.ts` is recorded by another backend file. No activation named (an account's first `app.*` event counts) and a package kind say nothing.

| Capability | Title | In dev | Under `--prod` | `--fix` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analytics` | Activation event | Warns, never fails | Still a warning | No |

**Why it matters:** The growth funnel counts a person's activation when that event is recorded for them. A kind nothing records leaves the activation step at zero ([Measure growth](/docs/build/growth/measure#name-your-activation-event)). **Fix:** Record the kind where a person first gets value, with `audit.recordBackendEvent(ctx, { type })`, or name the kind you already record. Check it again with `npx nuxt-backend doctor --only analytics`.

site-https.title: HTTPS and HSTS
site-https.entry:
### `site-https`

An anonymous request to the root of production's site, at the `https` origin its `SITE_URL` names, following its redirects: answered at that origin, with `Strict-Transport-Security` for a day or more. A redirect to plain HTTP fails; a redirect to another origin, no HSTS, a shorter one or a `5xx` warns. A site that was not probed at all is one warning, on the first probe the run checks (this one, else `site-gated-page`, `mcp-challenge` or `monitoring-health`), and no other probe runs: a site that does not answer, or, in a run without the auth capability, whose `site-url-origin` would say so, a `SITE_URL` that names no `https` origin of its own.

| Capability | Title | In dev | Under `--prod` | `--fix` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hosting` | HTTPS and HSTS | Not checked | Fails when the root redirects to plain HTTP; otherwise warns | No |

**Why it matters:** Without HTTPS, sessions and sign-in codes cross the network in the clear; without HSTS, a browser may try plain HTTP first; on another origin, the browser holds sessions and passkeys for an origin auth does not trust. **Fix:** Serve the app over HTTPS at the origin `SITE_URL` names, and keep the security headers on (nuxt-security, which the module registers, sends HSTS for 180 days). Check it again with `npx nuxt-backend doctor --only hosting --prod`.

site-csp.title: Content security policy
site-csp.entry:
### `site-csp`

The root's `Content-Security-Policy`: in every policy it holds (a header sent twice, by the app and by the host or a proxy, is two, and browsers enforce each), `connect-src` (else `default-src`) lets the browser reach the deployment the page talks to and its WebSocket twin (`https://<slug>.convex.cloud` and `wss://<slug>.convex.cloud`), as browsers match sources: an exact origin, a `*.` host, a scheme, `*`. A gap fails; a WebSocket let through only by its `https` origin's source warns (current browsers connect, some older engines do not); no policy at all warns. A page that names no deployment URL (a custom domain for the deployment) leaves the policy unjudged, and `site-backend-url` warns.

| Capability | Title | In dev | Under `--prod` | `--fix` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hosting` | Content security policy | Not checked | Fails when the policy blocks the deployment or its WebSocket; otherwise warns | No |

**Why it matters:** A policy that blocks the deployment blocks every query, mutation and realtime update in the browser; with no policy, an injected script may send data anywhere. **Fix:** The module adds the deployment the page talks to (its runtime config) to `connect-src` of the security headers' `/**` rule, so a gap comes from elsewhere: a policy the app host or a proxy adds, a route rule more specific than `/**` that sets its own `connect-src`, or the module's policy turned off (`contentSecurityPolicy: false`) with one set elsewhere. Add the deployment's `https://` and `wss://` origins there ([Security](/docs/ship/security)). Check it again with `npx nuxt-backend doctor --only hosting --prod`.

site-backend-url.title: Backend the site uses
site-backend-url.entry:
### `site-backend-url`

The deployment the root page names in its inlined runtime config is production's (the URL `convex function-spec --prod` reports). Another deployment's URL (dev's, after a build with `.env.local`) fails; no deployment URL at all (a custom domain for the deployment) warns.

| Capability | Title | In dev | Under `--prod` | `--fix` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hosting` | Backend the site uses | Not checked | Fails when the page talks to another deployment; otherwise warns | No |

**Why it matters:** An app built against dev serves production's visitors dev's data, signs them in there, and bills them nowhere. **Fix:** Build the app against production: set `NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL` in the app host's production env to production's deployment, or build with `npx convex deploy --cmd 'npm run build' --cmd-url-env-var-name NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL`; then redeploy the app ([Deployment](/docs/ship/deploy)). Check it again with `npx nuxt-backend doctor --only hosting --prod`.

agent-docs.title: Docs for agents
agent-docs.entry:
### `agent-docs`

Production's `/llms.txt`, where the app serves docs for agents (nuxt-llms configured, as Docus does, or listed as a module): a text document that starts with a heading passes; anything else warns. An app that neither declares nor serves it gets no finding.

| Capability | Title | In dev | Under `--prod` | `--fix` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hosting` | Docs for agents | Not checked | Warns, never fails | No |

**Why it matters:** Coding agents read `/llms.txt` to learn the app's docs; a declared one that is missing points them at nothing. **Fix:** Check the `llms` options in nuxt.config, and that the build ran its module. Check it again with `npx nuxt-backend doctor --only hosting --prod`.

AUTH_SECRET.takes: a random secret of at least 32 characters (`openssl rand -base64 32` prints one)
AUTH_SECRET.without: a deploy fails: it signs sessions and encrypts the keys the session tokens are signed with

SITE_URL.takes: the app's http(s) origin, without a path
SITE_URL.without: a deploy fails: auth trusts it as the app origin, and every emailed link names it

BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT.takes: `development`, `preview`, `sandbox` or `production`: the kind of deployment the backend runs on. `env push` derives it from the deployment; `sandbox` is the one value you set by hand
BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT.without: every provider stays in its test mode, nothing local is trusted and no sign-in code is logged; `doctor --prod` fails on production

EMAIL_API_KEY.without: email sends no-op; on `development` the sign-in codes print in the dev console, and elsewhere a code to a real address is refused

EMAIL_FROM.takes: an address on a verified sending domain, alone or as `Name <address>`: the sender of transactional mail
EMAIL_FROM.without: the provider onboarding sender is used

EMAIL_MARKETING_FROM.takes: an address on a sending subdomain apart from EMAIL_FROM's, alone or as `Name <address>`: the sender of marketing and lifecycle mail

EMAIL_REGION.takes: the region the sending domain sends from: `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `sa-east-1` or `ap-northeast-1`. Account data stays in the US whatever the region

EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET.takes: the signing secret of the provider's webhook endpoint; it verifies `/email/events`
EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET.without: delivery events are rejected — useEmailStatus stays at "sent"

EMAIL_DEV_INBOX.takes: `1` publishes the dev inbox to pages: getSandboxInbox answers on a deployment whose BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT is set and not production. `nuxt-backend dev` sets it on dev deployments and `nuxt-backend deploy --sandbox` on a sandbox (a public demo, whose visitors read their codes off the page); set it by hand on a preview that publishes the inbox, and never on a live production, where `doctor --prod` flags it
EMAIL_DEV_INBOX.without: the dev inbox's page reader (getSandboxInbox, behind useSandboxInbox) answers nothing; the CLI's inbox still reads

BILLING_ACCESS_TOKEN.takes: an organization access token of the billing provider: a sandbox token outside production, a live one on it
BILLING_ACCESS_TOKEN.without: billing queries return empty and checkout actions fail on invocation

BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET.takes: the signing secret of the provider's webhook endpoint (`billing sync` stores it); it verifies `/billing/events`
BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET.without: billing events are rejected — entitlements refresh only on demand (syncEntitlements)

AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.takes: a Vercel AI Gateway API key: the route a provider/model id takes where the Convex AI Gateway does not answer it. Convex runs actions on its own servers, never on Vercel, so the gateway's keyless sign-in never reaches them
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY.without: a provider/model id the backend names goes through the Convex AI Gateway alone, on Convex Cloud with a paid plan and @convex-dev/ai-sdk-provider installed; anywhere else (a free plan, a self-hosted deployment) it is refused when called

PROVENANCE_PRIVATE_KEY.takes: the PKCS #8 PEM key (`BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`, P-256, P-384 or RSA) that signs the content credentials `ctx.storeImage` writes, its line ends escaped as `\n` on one line. `env push` generates one with PROVENANCE_CERTIFICATE when neither the deployment nor .env.local has it and the backend turns provenance on
PROVENANCE_PRIVATE_KEY.without: generated images are stored with the IPTC source type and no signed C2PA manifest (`ai.provenance_unsigned`); `doctor --prod` fails once the backend turns provenance on

PROVENANCE_CERTIFICATE.takes: the PEM certificate chain of PROVENANCE_PRIVATE_KEY, the signer's certificate first: one `env push` issues under a root of its own (verifiers show its signer as unknown), or one from a certificate authority on the C2PA trust list for a named signer
PROVENANCE_CERTIFICATE.without: as without PROVENANCE_PRIVATE_KEY: the two sign together

PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY.takes: the public half of the web push (VAPID) key pair, base64url (an uncompressed P-256 point). Browsers receive it when they subscribe, so it is public. `env push` generates the pair when neither the deployment nor .env.local has it, and `env push --prod` a pair of production's own, never copied from .env.local. Never derived from another secret: new keys orphan every subscribed device
PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY.without: the in-app inbox and email notifications work, but web push does not: `getPushConfig` answers no key, so `usePushSubscription` reads unsupported

PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY.takes: the private half of the same pair, base64url (the 32-byte P-256 scalar). It stays on the deployment, never in the app's public config
PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY.without: as without PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY: the two sign together

PROTECTION_PROOF_SECRET.takes: a random secret of at least 32 characters (`openssl rand -base64 32` prints one), the same value on the deployment and on the app's server, and production's its own, never .env.local's. For an app on Vercel, where BotID signs the proofs: off Vercel nothing signs one, so set it there only beside the challenge keys. The app's server reads it from .env.local in development; in production set it in the host's env by hand. Never derived from another secret: to rotate it, a comma-separated `new,old` on the deployment passes proofs signed with either
PROTECTION_PROOF_SECRET.without: the auth routes that send a code take no proof of a bot check: on Vercel, BotID still refuses the bots that come through the app, but not the ones that call the deployment's own URL

PROTECTION_CHALLENGE_SECRET_KEY.takes: the challenge provider's secret key (Cloudflare Turnstile); its documented test keys pass or refuse everyone
PROTECTION_CHALLENGE_SECRET_KEY.without: the deployment verifies no challenge answer, so off Vercel nothing checks for bots

MONITORING_DSN.takes: a DSN of the monitoring service (`https://<key>@<host>/<project id>`). The Nuxt app reads it too. Where the service's Vercel integration sets the DSN as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, the app reads that, and `env push` forwards it as `MONITORING_DSN`, so the integration alone is enough
MONITORING_DSN.without: the backend reports nothing: errors in its actions and its cron check-ins go nowhere (the browser and the Nuxt server report on the DSN the app reads, and in dev a local error log stands in)

NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL.without: derived from the deployment the platform CLI names in .env.local; set it to point at another deployment

NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_CHALLENGE_SITE_KEY.takes: the challenge provider's site key (Cloudflare Turnstile), public. Its documented test keys (`1x00000000000000000000AA` always passes) are test mode
NUXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_CHALLENGE_SITE_KEY.without: no challenge widget renders, so the deployment's PROTECTION_CHALLENGE_SECRET_KEY refuses every code request that carries no proof

useAuth.summary: Who is signed in: the session, the app-wide role, whether an administrator is visiting, and signing out.

useConnectionState.summary: The live connection to the deployment, under a neutral name for the base module's.

useBackendClient.summary: The imperative client, under a neutral name for the base module's.

useLoginFlow.summary: The headless login flow behind `<AuthForm>` — bring your own markup and wire these refs/actions to it.

useEmailChange.summary: The headless email change behind `<ProfileSettings>`: a code from the current address proves the person asking still holds it, a code from the new address proves they hold that one too.

useWorkspace.summary: Workspace state and actions: the list, the switch, the members and the full invitation flow (invite / accept / decline / cancel — the packaged `AcceptInvitation` component and `/accept-invitation` page build on these).

useBilling.summary: Reactive billing state plus the full subscription lifecycle — checkout, gift, portal, plan change and undoing a scheduled one, cancel/uncancel, pause/resume — linked to your auth user.

useFeatures.summary: Reactive feature-gating for the current user — the SaaS access primitive.

useCredits.summary: Reactive prepaid-credit balance for the current user, plus a `topUp()` checkout and a `refresh()` re-sync.

usePricing.summary: The app's plans and credit packs as a pricing page shows them — every plan with its monthly and yearly price, what a year saves, its trial and the credits it grants per cycle; every pack with its price per credit and which is the best value — read through the scaffolded `getPricing`, in the visitor's currency where the catalog prices it.

useCampaign.summary: The campaign a visitor arrived with, read from the address: a campaign link's discount code and its UTM attribution, ready for checkout.

useOrders.summary: The signed-in customer's billing history — past charges straight from the provider's orders API, plus the per-order invoice link.

useUsage.summary: Consumption history for a credit meter, read from the provider's events API — the events your server ingested when it spent credits.

useReferrals.summary: A person's referral code, link and rewards: the data behind `<ReferralCard>`, for a page of your own.

useReferralAdmin.summary: The admin console's Referrals tab, as data: the program's totals, the top referrers, the flagged queue and one referrer's history, through `backend/referrals.ts`, and the decision an administrator makes on a flagged referral.

usePasskeys.summary: Passkey management over the auth client — list, register, rename, remove.

useSessions.summary: Device-session management: list, revoke one, revoke the rest.

useReauthentication.summary: Asking the person to confirm it is them before a sensitive action: the client half of `requireRecentSignIn` and of the routes that take a recent sign-in.

useAuditLog.summary: The activity trail, a page at a time: the signed-in account's own (sign-ins, passkeys, email and session changes, workspaces joined, an administrator's actions on it), the active workspace's for its owners and admins, or every event for administrators.

useAccount.summary: The account itself: its profile, its export and its deletion.

useConsents.summary: What a signed-in person agreed to, and the consent manager for optional storage.

useAdmin.summary: The admin console's data and actions: a paged, searchable list of every account or every workspace, one account or workspace in full, and the administrator's actions on an account.

useFlag.summary: Whether a feature flag is on for whoever is looking: their account, their active workspace and their plan, as `backend/flags.ts` declares the flag and the admin console overrides it.

useFlagAdmin.summary: The admin console's Flags tab, as data: every flag with its default and its override, and the change an administrator makes, through `listFlags` and `setFlag` of `backend/flags.ts`.

useAccessPhase.summary: The app's launch phase, so a page offers what a visitor can do now: join the waitlist in early access, bring an invite code while invite only, sign up once public.

useInvite.summary: Redeem an invite code or an access link on a page of your own: check it before anyone signs in, and keep it for the tab so the sign-in hands it over with the code.

useAccessAdmin.summary: The admin console's Access tab, as data: the launch phase and its change, the invite codes and access links, and the invitations by address, through `backend/access.ts`.

useWaitlist.summary: Join the waitlist, and read a place in it, on markup of your own: the steps `<WaitlistForm>` runs.

useWaitlistAdmin.summary: The admin console's Waitlist tab, as data: the waiting people (the oldest first, narrowed by a filter) with a count per status, and the changes an administrator makes, through `backend/waitlist.ts`.

useShareLink.summary: One row's share link: whether it has a live one and since when, read live, and the actions that turn it on (or mint a new one) and off, through `getShareLink`, `enableShareLink` and `revokeShareLink` of `backend/storage.ts`.

useUploadField.summary: The upload field without its markup: pick a file (by the button or by dropping it), upload it with the base module's `useUpload` through the upload URL `setupStorage` mints, then hand the storage id to your `claim`, where the deployment checks it.

useNotifications.summary: The signed-in account's in-app notifications, live: newest first, paged with `loadMore`, with the unread count and the actions that mark them read.

useNotificationInbox.summary: `<NotificationInbox>` without its markup: the notifications, where the inbox is, the button's name with the unread count in it, and the bindings for a button and a list that open on the browser's own popover.

useEmailPreferences.summary: The email topics the signed-in person receives and their notification channels, kind by kind, live, and the actions that change them: the same choices as the profile's Email section, the unsubscribe page and the provider's own page, which all stay in step.

usePushSubscription.summary: Web push on this device, for the signed-in person: whether the browser can take it, whether this device is subscribed, the permission, and the actions that subscribe and unsubscribe it.

useAnnouncements.summary: The announcements an administrator published that the signed-in person has not dismissed, live: what `<BackendNotices>`' `announcement` notice shows.

useAnnouncementsAdmin.summary: The admin console's Announcements tab, as data: every announcement with its notice and its broadcast, and the changes an administrator makes, through `backend/email.ts`.

useContactForm.summary: The contact form without its markup: a name and an address for a visitor, the message alone for a signed-in account (so the same form on a page behind sign-in is a feedback form), the bot check, a honeypot, and the deployment's refusals.

useOnboarding.summary: The first run at `/welcome` without its markup: the steps in order, where the person is, moving between them, and the stamp that ends it.

useActivation.summary: The activation checklist without its markup: the first tasks `defineActivation` declares, which of them are done, the progress, and dismissing it.

useExperiment.summary: The variant of an experiment, a `defineFlags` flag with `variants`, for whoever is looking.

useAppShell.summary: The app shell without its markup: who is signed in, the links of the account menu, signing out, and the workspace switcher.

useInboxAdmin.summary: The admin console's Inbox tab, as data: what people sent through the contact form and by email (reply addresses, workspace addresses, the support inbox), newest first, and the replies an administrator sends to the support inbox's threads, through `backend/email.ts`.

getBackendError.summary: Read a refusal out of anything a call threw or resolved with: a `backendError()` from a Convex function, the rate limiter's own `RateLimited` error, an auth client's `{ data, error }` result or its `error`, a Better Auth `APIError`, and any of these as an `Error`'s `cause`.

useBackendConfig.summary: `appConfig.backend` with the package defaults merged in — the shipped components read content (plan catalog, labels, brand) through this, so a partial user config is always safe to destructure.

useLabels.summary: The labels of one packaged component's group, resolved for the person reading them.

useBackendPagePath.summary: Where a ready-made page lives, for a link to it: the path the module mounted it at (the `pages` module option, else its default), in the active locale when the app uses `@nuxtjs/i18n` (through its `localePath`, so `/pricing` reads `/fr/pricing` under a prefix strategy).

useReturnPath.summary: Where the person goes once a page that interrupted them is done: the page they were headed for, from the `?redirect=` the sign-in and the first-run redirect carry (kept to a path on this site, so a link can never send them elsewhere), else where sign-in lands (`redirects.afterSignIn`, `/` without it).

useEmailStatus.summary: Reactive delivery status for a sent email.

useSandboxInbox.summary: The mail a test address received within the last hour, refreshed while the page is open — so a demo, a preview deployment or an e2e run can finish an email-code sign-in without a real mailbox.

useAiStream.summary: Drive a metered, persisted AI text stream (an `ai.stream(...)` definition from `nuxt-backend/ai`).

useJob.summary: One queued job, live: its status, what holds it and its place in line while it waits, its progress while it runs, and its result or the reason it failed.

useAiLabel.summary: The AI-generated label without its markup: its words, and with a provenance record the details it opens — the models, the date and a link to check the content credentials — as state and bindings.

useChat.summary: A chat with a model, live: the person's threads, the open thread's messages with the reply streaming into them, and sending.

useHumanCheck.summary: Proof that a person makes a call: the client half of `verifyHuman`, for the calls that reach the deployment over the live connection and never pass through the app's server (a waitlist join, a contact form, a referral claim).

AuthForm.summary: The complete passwordless sign-in flow (passkeys + email OTP) in one component: semantic markup where every element carries a `data-auth` attribute, built from parts (`AuthFormChoose`, `AuthFormCode`, …) that a same-named component of the app's replaces, and a slot per step.
AuthForm.entry:
## `<AuthForm>`

The complete passwordless sign-in flow (passkeys + email OTP) in one component: semantic markup where every element carries a `data-auth` attribute, built from parts (`AuthFormChoose`, `AuthFormCode`, …) that a same-named component of the app's replaces, and a slot per step.

| At a glance |  |
|---|---|
| Registered from | `src/runtime/vue/components/auth/AuthForm.vue` |
| Rendered by | the `/login` page (`pages.login`) |
| Family | `data-auth` |
| Labels | [`auth`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#auth) |
| Slots | `header`, `choose`, `request-code`, `verify-code`, `passkey-offer`, `recover`, `waitlisted`, `invite-code`, `age`, `undeliverable`, `error`, `footer` |
| Events | `success`, `error`, `step` |
| States | ready, request-code, verify-code, passkey-offer, recover, waitlisted, invite-code, age, undeliverable, pending, error |
| Parts | `AuthFormHeader`, `AuthFormChoose`, `AuthFormPasskey`, `AuthFormEmail`, `AuthFormCode`, `AuthFormRecover`, `AuthFormWaitlisted`, `AuthFormInviteCode`, `AuthFormAge`, `AuthFormUndeliverable`, `AuthFormPasskeyOffer`, `AuthFormAgreement`, `AuthFormError` |
| Tier | stable |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | none | Heading text. Defaults to the `auth.title` label an app set, then "Sign in to {brand.name}", then "Sign in"; an empty string hides it. |
| `labels` | `LabelOverrides<BackendLabels['auth']>` | none | Copy for this form, over `appConfig.backend.labels.auth` and the translations. |
| `validateEmail` | `(email: string) => boolean \| string` | none | Gate emails before sending (`true` \| `false` \| custom message). Default: a basic shape check. |

**Accessibility:** Focus moves to the new step's first control when the person moved the form on, and stays put on the step it opens on; a busy button keeps focus (`aria-disabled`) and says what it waits for; a refused field is `aria-invalid` and described by the refusal; the "Last used" mark describes its button and adds no stop; the sent-code note and the passkey offer are polite statuses, a failure an alert; the email field autocompletes as `username webauthn`, where the browser offers saved passkeys, and codes as one-time codes; the age question has a visible label and an empty field and never names the minimum, and the agreement line links each required document; an address the provider stopped delivering to reads as an alert, with the same words for every address, and a button back to the email field.

WaitlistForm.summary: Join the waitlist: the address, your questions, the launch-news box (unticked), then the sign-in code that proves the address, then the person's place, a link to share and a way to leave.
WaitlistForm.entry:
## `<WaitlistForm>`

Join the waitlist: the address, your questions, the launch-news box (unticked), then the sign-in code that proves the address, then the person's place, a link to share and a way to leave. It runs the steps of `useWaitlist()` and renders one slot per step (`join`, `verify`, `status`), each given that object, around the parts `WaitlistJoin`, `WaitlistCode` and `WaitlistPlace` (which renders `WaitlistShare`), each replaced everywhere by a same-named component of the app's. A friend's link the visitor came through is shown beside the form, and can be dropped.

| At a glance |  |
|---|---|
| Registered from | `src/runtime/vue/components/auth/WaitlistForm.vue` |
| Rendered by | no ready-made page: place it yourself |
| Family | `data-waitlist` |
| Labels | [`waitlist`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#waitlist) |
| Slots | `join`, `verify`, `status` |
| Events | `joined`, `signed-in`, `left`, `error` |
| States | ready, verify-code, waitlisted, pending, error |
| Parts | `WaitlistJoin`, `WaitlistCode`, `WaitlistPlace`, `WaitlistShare` |
| Tier | stable |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` | `LabelGroupOverrides<'waitlist'>` | none | Copy for this component, over `appConfig.backend.labels.waitlist` and the translations. |
| `source` | `string` | none | Where this form is, for the Source column of the Waitlist tab (letters, digits and `. : / - _`). Default `form`. |
| `questionLabels` | `Record<string, string>` | none | What to show for each of your questions: its text, by key. Without one, the key is shown. |
| `shareTo` | `string` | none | Where a friend's link points: this form's page. Default: the page it is on. |

**Accessibility:** Every field has a visible label, and the launch-news box is unticked until the person ticks it; the sent-code note is a polite status, a refusal an alert that the refused field is described by and marks `aria-invalid`; a busy button keeps focus (`aria-disabled`) and says what it waits for, and the wrapper is `aria-busy`; the place is a polite status that reads in words, the honest words about admission sit beside it, and the share link is a labelled read-only field with a copy button; no names and no leaderboards are ever shown.

ReauthenticateDialog.summary: "Confirm it's you": the dialog a sensitive action opens when the server refuses it as `reauthentication_required`.
ReauthenticateDialog.entry:
## `<ReauthenticateDialog>`

"Confirm it's you": the dialog a sensitive action opens when the server refuses it as `reauthentication_required`. The person signs in again with a passkey, or with a code emailed to the account's own address, and the action runs once more (`useReauthentication().withReauthentication`). The code request passes the bot check as the sign-in form's does: when the challenge asks for a click, its widget shows inside this dialog, where the person can reach it.

| At a glance |  |
|---|---|
| Registered from | `src/runtime/vue/components/auth/ReauthenticateDialog.vue` |
| Rendered by | the `/admin` page (`pages.admin`) and the `/security` page (`pages.security`), inside their components |
| Family | `data-reauthenticate` |
| Labels | [`reauthenticate`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#reauthenticate) |
| Slots | `choose`, `verify-code`, `error`, `footer` |
| Events | `reauthenticated`, `cancelled`, `error`, `step` |
| States | empty, ready, verify-code, pending, error |
| Parts | `ReauthenticatePasskey`, `ReauthenticateCode` |
| Tier | stable |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` | `LabelOverrides<BackendLabels['reauthenticate']>` | none | Copy for this dialog, over `appConfig.backend.labels.reauthenticate` and the translations. |

**Accessibility:** A native modal dialog named by its heading: it opens on its first control, keeps focus inside, closes on Escape or "Cancel", and gives focus back to the control that opened it; the code field has a visible label, autocompletes as a one-time code and is described by the sent-code note, a polite status; a busy button keeps focus (`aria-disabled`) and says what it waits for; a failure is an alert. Nothing renders until a sensitive action asks.

ProfileSettings.summary: Account profile: identity chrome (avatar initials, verification / role / workspace badges), display-name editing, the email change, by a code from each address, and, with `@nuxtjs/i18n` and two locales or more, the person's language, which their emails are written in.
ProfileSettings.entry:
## `<ProfileSettings>`

Account profile: identity chrome (avatar initials, verification / role / workspace badges), display-name editing, the email change, by a code from each address, and, with `@nuxtjs/i18n` and two locales or more, the person's language, which their emails are written in. Identity renders client-only — session state differs between SSR and hydration.

| At a glance |  |
|---|---|
| Registered from | `src/runtime/vue/components/account/ProfileSettings.vue` |
| Rendered by | the `/profile` page (`pages.profile`) |
| Family | `data-profile` |
| Labels | [`profile`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#profile) |
| Slots | `identity`, `name`, `email`, `language`, `preferences`, `footer` |
| Events | `name-saved`, `email-changed`, `error` |
| States | ready, confirm-current, pending, error |
| Parts | `ProfileIdentity`, `ProfileNameSection`, `ProfileEmailSection`, `ProfileLanguageSection`, `ProfilePreferencesSection` |
| Tier | stable |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `validateEmail` | `(email: string) => boolean \| string` | none | Gate the new email before any code is sent (`true` \| `false` \| custom message). Default: a basic shape check. |
| `showIdentity` | `boolean` | `true` |  |

## `<Gate>`

**Accessibility:** The field is named by its visible label; the picker is a button that opens the browser's own file dialog, so the keyboard path needs no drop; while a file uploads it shows a labelled progress bar and a Cancel button, and the field is `aria-busy`; each step (uploading, checking, done, canceled) is said in a polite status, and a refusal is an alert the input is described by.

NotificationInbox.summary: What the app told a person, in the app: a button whose accessible name carries the unread count, and the list it opens on the browser's own popover, newest first.
NotificationInbox.entry:
## `<NotificationInbox>`

What the app told a person, in the app: a button whose accessible name carries the unread count, and the list it opens on the browser's own popover, newest first. Opening a notification marks it read; the list marks every one read at once and loads older ones on request. Every event the backend records about the person reaches it live, worded in the active language, with nothing to wire per kind. Renders nothing for a signed-out visitor, or while an administrator acts as the account. The logic is `useNotificationInbox`, so markup of your own can do the same with its bindings.

| At a glance |  |
|---|---|
| Registered from | `src/runtime/vue/components/shell/NotificationInbox.vue` |
| Rendered by | no ready-made page: place it yourself |
| Family | `data-notifications` |
| Labels | [`notifications`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#notifications) |
| Slots | `notification`, `empty` |
| Events | none |
| States | ready, loading, empty, error, pending, refused |
| Parts | `NotificationInboxBell`, `NotificationInboxItem` |
| Tier | stable |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `number` | none | Notifications per page, at most 50. Default 20. |
| `labels` | `LabelGroupOverrides<'notifications'>` | none | Copy for this inbox, over app config and the translations. |

**Accessibility:** The button's accessible name carries the unread count ("Notifications, 3 unread"), and the badge beside it is hidden from assistive technology so the count is not read twice; the list is a non-modal popover named by its heading, which the browser closes on Escape and light dismiss and returns focus from to the button; an unread notification says so in a hidden word beside the dot, a notification without a place to go is a button that marks it read, and the first page loads in a polite status, an empty inbox says so in one, and a failure is an alert. A signed-out visitor gets nothing to press.

ContactForm.summary: A contact form for visitors, and a feedback form for signed-in people: the same component.
ContactForm.entry:
## `<ContactForm>`

A contact form for visitors, and a feedback form for signed-in people: the same component. Signed out it asks for a name, an address to answer and a message; signed in it sends as the account and asks for the message alone. The deployment checks the message, a hidden honeypot field and the bot check, limits each sender, and stores the message before anything is sent to your team. The form never emails the address someone typed: the confirmation is the form itself. The logic is `useContactForm`, so markup of your own can do the same with its bindings. Needs `submitContactMessage` re-exported from `email.api` in `backend/email.ts`.

| Rendered by | no ready-made page: place it yourself |
| Family | `data-contact` |
| Labels | [`contact`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#contact) |
| Slots | `fields`, `sent`, `error` |
| Events | `sent`, `error` |
| States | ready, pending, sent, error, refused |
| Parts | none: swap the whole component |
| Tier | stable |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` | `LabelGroupOverrides<'contact'>` | none | Copy for this form, over app config and the translations. |

**Accessibility:** Every field has a visible label, and the message is described by a line that gives its length range and count; the honeypot is hidden from people and from assistive technology; the send button stays focused while the message is on its way (`aria-disabled`) and says so; a persistent polite live region announces the sending and the confirmation, and a refusal is an alert the field it names is described by, worded to say what to do next.

AppShell.summary: The frame of a signed-in app, for your layout: a header with your brand and links, the workspace switcher, the notification bell and the account menu, then the app-wide notices, then your page in the `<main>` landmark, with the consent dialog and the connection status closing it.
AppShell.entry:
## `<AppShell>`

The frame of a signed-in app, for your layout: a header with your brand and links, the workspace switcher, the notification bell and the account menu, then the app-wide notices, then your page in the `<main>` landmark, with the consent dialog and the connection status closing it. Signed out it shows your brand, your links and a sign-in link. The menus are disclosures on the browser's native popover, placed with CSS anchor positioning. The packaged pages inside it leave the header, the notices and the landmark to the shell. The logic is `useAppShell`.

| At a glance |  |
|---|---|
| Registered from | `src/runtime/vue/components/shell/AppShell.vue` |
| Rendered by | no ready-made page: place it yourself |
| Family | `data-shell` |
| Labels | [`shell`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#shell) |
| Slots | `brand`, `nav`, `actions`, `default` |
| Events | none |
| States | ready, loading, refused |
| Parts | `AccountMenu`, `WorkspaceSwitcher` |
| Tier | stable |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `switcher` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the workspace switcher. Turn it off in an app whose people never share a workspace. Read when the shell is set up. |
| `labels` | `LabelGroupOverrides<'shell'>` | none | Copy for the shell, over `appConfig.backend.labels.shell` and the translations. |

**Accessibility:** The first stop is a skip link to the page; the header is the one banner landmark, the app's links sit in a navigation landmark named by the `navigation` label, and the page is the one `main` landmark. The account menu and the workspace switcher are disclosures on the browser's own popover: the button names the account or the workspace first and says what it opens, Escape or a click outside closes the panel and focus returns to the button, and the open state is `aria-expanded`. The current workspace is `aria-current` and says so in words, a role is a word and never a colour, and a switch, a creation and a sign-out are said in a polite status, a failure in an alert. A busy button keeps focus (`aria-disabled`).

AiLabel.summary: The visible "AI-generated" label the EU AI Act (Art.
AiLabel.entry:
## `<AiLabel>`

The visible "AI-generated" label the EU AI Act (Art. 50) asks for, beside an image or a text a model made. Alone, it is the label; with a `provenance` record (`useJob().provenance`, `ai.provenanceOf`), the label is a button that opens its details: the models, the date, and a link to check the image's content credentials.

| Rendered by | no ready-made page: place it yourself |
| Family | `data-ai-label` |
| Labels | [`ai`](/docs/reference/configuration/labels#ai) |

**Props**

| Prop | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provenance` | `JobProvenance \| null` | none | What made the content: with it, the label opens its details. |

**Accessibility:** Plain text that says the content is AI-generated, never a colour or an icon alone; with a provenance record it is a button that opens its details as a native popover (opened and closed by the keyboard, Escape closing it and focus returning to the button), a dialog named by its heading, whose verify link says where it goes.
